The economy of the NBE is a very diverse in terms of what it's makeup is and what it produces. Primary, secondary and tertiary sectors are abundant and common within the Empire with each province having vastly different makeups unique to it's geographic position and political history. Private property is effectively guaranteed although all land is technically "leased" out by the Emperor himself. Foreign companies are permitted to operate within the Empire, albeit that they accept the dominance of Balionic companies in terms of logistics (IE, transport companies) and have a local subsidiary headquartered within the Empire or else foreign companies face higher tariffs and legal prohibitions. Tariffs exist as a baseline for all foreign companies but are reduced depending on how rare their product/service is within the Empire and/or if a local subsidiary is set up. 

Foreign investment is very much welcomed, especially in the booming cities of the Empire, where skyscrapers are rapidly being built and the frontier regions of the Empire which seek settlers and investment. Assets can be seized if deemed that the foreign nation is a threat (IE, at war like is the case with Gaesun) and/or dominate over local companies, individuals and aristocratic claims. But such seizures are rare considering the legal benefits natives have and that in the cases that certain areas need investment, they will likely have to be dealt in a court.

[spoiler=Chaos ensues as brawl breaks out inside the Diet!]
[i]Wellassonan National News - Новеллсти Нациоьнлыы Веласоньый. Sunday, 4 June 2028[/i]

Earlier today, a shocking and unprecedented scene broke out in the Wellassonan Diet, as shoves, pushes, and even punches were exchanged between various members of Wellassona's lower house.

The prelude to the incident was rooted in complex, partisan conflict that has arisen in the past few years. During the premiership of Socialist Danik Sokolova, the Socialists have come under heavy scrutiny for their economic policies, as many people see them as extremely draconic and illiberal. While Sokolova defends his policies, describing them as necessary to counter the [i]"robber-barons"[/i] of the big industry, many fellow Socialists have also come to view his economic agenda as unnecessarily cruel. The unpopularity for said economic policies has been a major factor in the rise of the Reform the State Party, led by Valya Kulikov. The far-right party has seen unprecedented growth in the past decade. Their agenda is descrided as being Nationalistic, anti-immigration (especially from Muslim countries), anti-LGBT, anti-abortion, laissez-faire, climate change denialist, and autarkic. This has led to the party being ostracised by the other parties, as they view them with extreme suspicion. This is especially true for the Socialists, with Sokolova himself calling them [i]"dirty fascists"[/i] on multiple occasions. This animosity is shared by Reform the State, with Kulikov calling Sokolova a [i]"communist demagogue"[/i] and the Socialists the [i]"radical left"[/i].

All these tensions between the two parties had apparently met its breaking point earlier today. The Diet was convening, as it did every 2 weeks, to discuss and ratify bills to become laws. While the atmosphere was clearly tense, it wasn't perceivably palpable by any means. However, that clearly changed when the controversial [i]"Assurances of the Rights and Freedoms of Religious, Ethnic, and Sexual Minorities"[/i] bill was brought to discussion by inkenan Socialist diet member Rusul Abdeslam. The bill, contemptuously dubbed the [i]"Minorities First"[/i] bill by its opponents, aims to heavily increase anti-discrimination laws against people based on race, sex, ethnicity, and orientation. This bill arose following various reports of increasing discrimination against minority groups, particularly Muslims. While being supported by the Socialist and the People's Party, Reform the State vehemently oppose the bill, stating it to be [i]"highly unnecessary"[/i] given Wellassona's current circumstances, and that [i]"all it does is hypocritically takes away rights of people just to give them to others."[/i]

As Abdeslam promotes the bill, Rodya Diomid, the sole Reform the State diet member from Lomeckyj, unexpectedly interrupts him. Diomid begins to go on a filibuster, beginning to discuss the drawbacks of the bill. Before he can do so, Abdeslam interupts him back, telling him [i]"It's quite rude to interrupt someone."[/i] Annoyed, Diomid replies [i]"Fine, commie, let's see you talk the talk."[/i] Take aback by this, Abdeslam replies [i]"Oh I will, you ruffian."[/i] He then proceeds to talk about the merits of the bill, while Diomid is seen whispering to his fellow Reform the State Diet members next to him. After Abdeslam is finished speaking, Diomid stands up and claps, exclaiming [i]"Wonderfully Said!"[/i] in a sarcastic tone. Hearing this, Abdeslam mutters, [i]"F*ck you"[/i], to which Diomid replies [i]"Hey! Let's keep this discussion family-friendly, Okay bud?"[/i] He continues on with his filibuster. However, instead of respectfully discussing the bill as he had previously attempted to, he decried it heavily, calling it [i]"a radical-left plot to put down the everyday Wellassonan to curry favour with minorities,"[/i] and a [i]"hot piece of communist-infused horse-sh*t."[/i] Already incensed, Abdeslam intrrupted Diomid again, and the feud continued as followed:

Abdeslam:[i]I thought you told me to keep it family friendly?[/i]
Diomid:[i] I did, just to you.[/i]
Abdeslam:[i] You hypocrite! You have no reason to disrespect me like this![/i]
Diomid:[i] You have no reason to disrespect Wellassona like you do every day.[/i]
Abdeslam:[i] I have never disrespected this country! I Love this country![/i]
Diomid:[i] Say that to all the Wellassonans who fall victim to crimes committed by immigrants who flock to our country every single day without fail.[/i]
Abdeslam:[i] Now you are the one disrespecting Wellassona! You Racist![/i]
Diomid:[i] Hah! You call me racist? You only care about 14% of our people! And you're the one to call me racist?[/i]
Abdeslam:[i] Well, now your Islamophobia is clear to all, I hope you enjoy how people see the real you.[/i]
Diomid:[i] Let's wait for a terror attack to take place, and then we'll see who's talking then! [/i]

Abdeslam, a Muslim who's family immigrated to Wellassona when he was 6 and a strong advocate against Islamophobia, clearly enraged at Diomid's insensitive remark, got up from his seat and started walking towards Diomid's. Seeing this, Diomid sneered [i]"See? It's happening sooner than we thought."[/i] Just after he said this, Abdeslam pushed Diomid, who nearly lost his footing. Diomid instinctively pushed back, and was subsequently shoved to the ground by Abdeslam. At this, Other Reform the State diet members rushed to Diomid's aid, and began pushing Abdeslam right back. Quickly, some of the other Socialists went to help Abdeslam, and before long, pandemonium had taken over the Diet floor. The brawl quickly escalated between the Socialist and Reform the State Diet members, with screaming, pushing, shoving, and, intermittently, several punches. The security forces were hapless at stopping the mayhem, so the police were called to disperse the Diet members. During all this, the Diet members from all other parties either remained seated, watching in astonishment at the situation, or fleeing the Diet floor.

Abdeslam was charged with Assault and Battery against Diomid, While Diomid, 17 other Reform the State Diet members, and 26 Socialist Diet members, were also charged with either Assault, Battery, or both. Diomid was also charged with [i]"Racially-Motivated, Insensitive, and Demeaning Remarks"[/i] due to his comment regarding Muslims and terror attacks, which is what almost certainly prompted Abdeslam to engage physically with him. It is likely that many of the Diet members will face severe repercussions, depending on their degree of participation in the brawl, with many likely to be booted from the diet and replaced, or worse, face fines and jail time.

The incident was unprecedented and took the nation by surprise. Never in Wellassonan history had such an altercation taken place in the halls of the People's Assembly. Unsurprisingly, accusations and condemnations came flying in from both sides. Prime Minister Danil Sokolova expressed extreme concern at the incident, calling it [i]"horrifying." [/i]He subsequently condemned Diomid, calling him a [i]"bona fide Islamophobe who has no remorse for his appalling remarks."[/i] Kaldangan Kemurtevič the leader of the Socialists in the Diet, called the fight [i]"very depressing to see" saying, [i]"it saddened me to witness my comrades fight right in front of me."[/i] He also deplored Diomid's actions, saying, [i]"As a Muslim myself, Diomid's statements can only be called one thing: Hateful."[/i] When asked about Abdeslam's behaviour, he called it [i]"rather immature and reckless,"[/i] but also said that it was [i]"completely understandable given the abuse he received."[/i] On the other side, Kemder Premier Karina Lagounov, said the fight was [i]"more clear examples of left-wing violence seeping into our government and livelihoods."[/i] She proceeded to call Abdeslam a [i]"terrorist"[/i] and that [i]"He should be deported immediately".[/i] Reform the State Leader Valya Kulikov called the fight [i]"Concerning to watch"[/i] and that [i]"Pinning the blame on the victims is not what should be done at the moment."[/i] She decried Abdeslam as a [i]"disgrace to his nation"[/i] and lauded Diomid as a [i]"martyr."[/i] The Reform the State party stated in an official statement that they would [i]"investigate"[/i] Diomid's remarks on Muslims, stating [i]"We always to wish to support the equality between every citizen of our great nation. We oppose Islamophobia and will thoroughly look into Diomid's statements to examine any possible offence within it, and take action if we find it necessary to do so." [/i]

The cause célèbre comes at a time of already high sectarian tensions between the left and the right. There is no doubt that the brawl will have an effect on the upcoming General Elections on 29 July. Sokolova has already ordered there be greater security at both Senate and Diet convening to prevent anything remotely close to this from happening ever again. It is unclear how the brawl will effect the international perception of Wellassona, especially in a such a crucial time, as Wellassona has only just started opening up to the world in terms of international diplomacy.
[/spoiler]

[spoiler=[b]Unité[/b]][b]Unité
[sub]by "Auberjonois"[/sub][/b]

It is fundamentally righteous to perceive all existence as emanations derived from a single merciful Creator. In secular matters, we are also beholden to the knowledge given to us from the shoulders of giants. One such knowledge is the prerogative that all men are created equal, and who is believed (at least in academia) to have first emerged out of the Shamats and spread to all Erene.

Therefore all men, such as the Elseyran peoples, are no different from one another, even as our morphologies and linguistic characteristics may have shifted during the centuries that followed our emergence.

If we are certain, and we the faithful of the Holy Church shall always be certain, that life is equal, then any inquisitions about the real and perceived iniquities of the race of the Montfleurois and Rosenmarkket have been born out of ignorance to that Holy Church. We are different to the peoples that populated this land a thousand years ago, who held fast to the innate supremacy of lineage and pedigree, and who through that belief waged terrible wars in defense of feudatories and dynasties.

It was these wars that tore apart the Rosenmarkket and Montfleurois races. Still they tear the nations apart long after their battlefields have disappeared from our immediate memory.

Now, the time has come however for these nations to rejoin once again under a single banner and under a single identity. God has spoken to the people of the Rosenmarkket, whose experiments with independence and leftist radicalism have left only sorrow and destruction in their wake. Now He speaks to the Montfleurois too, appealing before them to lift their brothers and sisters out of ruin under the ancient and unifying banner once more.

The contest of unity is such that the Rosenmarkket and Montfleurois both maintain their reservations however as to the urgency of the great union. The Rosenmarkket fear a loss of identity, while the Montfleurois fear instability. Both concern themselves with the political and ideological risks that will certainly be brought upon by their divergent government systems, differently-structured welfare regimes, infrastructure, never mind geopolitical positioning. 

The Rosenmarkket have recently emerged out of their war in the White Straits with bruises and scars, yet now firmly aligned with the Socialist International. The Montfleurois, while well-acquainted with Sanguinian corporations, do not interest themselves in geopolitical rivalries.

Still there are other concerns, as with Rosenmarkke's aforementioned war, that has left the country under construction, both in military and in domestic affairs. Nominally, Rosenmarkke is economically larger than Montfleur, with several centuries of innovative progress that has enabled the growth of a substantial industrial and service-based sectors. Yet, its military capabilities have been severely compromised and is now scrambling to reassemble, all the while its disjointed soviets pursue localized and community-based projects to rapidly restore infrastructure. International markets remain skeptical, and some corporations fled for home in fear for their own investments, leaving opportunistic vultures such as the Vespurians to sweep in and try to forge their own corporate networks.

In Montfleur, the local population favors macroeconomic gradualism, and so have built from it an economy that is technologically-sophisticated and diversified, but also expensive. Since the abolition of feudalism, there has never been another revolution in Montfleur that sought to drastically rebuild its economic structure. The result of this is a vast network of old firms, some older than entire nations, that continue to operate in the old ways. Montfleur emphasizes technological innovation, and indeed in some respects it far surpasses Rosenmarkke in high-tech and knowledge-based industries, but this application is not universal. Farmers on the rural frontier retain traditional methods while manufacturing bases continue to use old systems, driving production costs without discernible benefits.

And yet, are these truly counterarguments against unification, or rather the problems that must now be surpassed in the great struggle thereto? No political unification in recent memory has ever been undertaken between perfectly co-equal and identical systems. The very basic foundation of unification is this endeavor to make seamless the joining of various institutions into the whole.

Now Rosenmarkke is divided, is there no finer opportunity yet that Montfleur might undertake to mend the tragedy of the 17th century? So long as the people are willing and the states capable, markets will eventually stabilize after the initial years of great effort. In the beginning, many in Montfleur will attempt to relocate en masse to reap the benefits of the wealthy south, while investments in the north will run dry, but there will be entrepeneurs and innovators, and in time we shall see these two halves of the Grande Montfleur stand shoulder to shoulder, but only if they dare to take the first step.[/spoiler]

[b]The History of East Elseyran Unity:[/b]

As the primary discussion in the previous papers has been based around modern-day unification theory, I have taken it upon myself to write a brief statement on the history of East Elseyran unity, which spans thousands of years, and provides significant material evidence in favor of a joyous reunion between Rosenmarkke and Montfleur.

[i]The Early Unitary States[/i]
The history of East Elseyran unity finds its place in the 1st century BC with the rise and solidification of the Marisalbic Empire, spanning from modern-day Montfleur to the borders of the modern-day Neue Republik. It remains at best the largest empire in the history of Erene, and its imperial method laid the groundwork for centuries of governance, with all nations on Elseyr deigning to claim a slice of inheritance. 

Following the fall of the Marisalbic empire in the 4th century AD, the lands of Elseyr were no longer conjoined to the west by a great empire, and, as the centuries darkened the face of Elseyr, the East and the West grew distant in all major affairs. However, by the time of the Middle Ages (these being from the 8th century to the 14th century by some historians), there arose a new form of unitarianist theory, primarily inspired in part by the remains of the Marisalbic system.

Under the compacts of the 9th and 10th centuries, the various fragmented kingdoms and duchies came to recognise heads and kingdoms more powerful than their own, seeking to unite with them to increase their own power. We see the early formation of the Eastern Elseyran states and monarchies that are present nowadays, namely that of Montfleur.

This Eastern unification under the early Montfleurois kings (known as the Alertian dynasty, rumored to be related to the ancient Marisalbic emperors) would see the restoration of the first unified kingdom since the fall of the Marisalbic empire, the kingdom grew in strength and power until we reach the 13th and 14th centuries when that power came to clash with the petty kingdoms and duchies of the White Sea, these namely being the merchant republic of Knygta and Deyn in the south, and the ever expanding Thrømm hetmanate, who had been written of by the Marisalbic writer Plutonis as being A hardy band of wilds, who live beyond the normal civilisation and will one day prove to either be a crucial ally or enemy to the affairs of the Marisalbic persons. 

It was in this region known as the Rosenmarkke that we see the first attempt of unity of which I shall now go into detail about.

[i]Rosenmarkke[/i]

The history of Rosenmarkke has been dominated by its geographic location on the White Sea, a crucial sea dividing the continents of Vespurias and Elseyr, and a major site for international and historic trade. The Peoples Republic of Rosenmarkke was formed in 1457 from the Kingdom of Montfleur, the Merchant Republic of Knygta, and the Thrømm Hetmanate as a defensive bloc against Llyndoran expansion and aggression against Montfleur. Following the fifty-year war from 1460-1500 and the successful expulsion of Llyndora from the historic Montfleurois territories of Lorraine, Gvenchy, and LaFleurisse, the three entities agreed to further cooperation between each other with Montfleurois king Charles Valian IV marrying the daughter of the doge of Knygta, Francesca Argenfioro in 1516. 

Unfortunately this era of grace and co-operation between the three powers would not last, with the Hemantate, concerned about expansions by the Merchant Republic into Hetmanate territory, formally declaring war in 1528 under the leadership of Dúrkos Erjk Samnäar. 

With the outbreak of war, the kingdom of Montfleur was placed in a rough position, between supporting the unity of the three states or defending the honour of the Merchant Republic, which provided a major financial back for Montfleur and was a crucial ally in the White Sea. Ultimately Charles IV would choose to come to the aid of the Merchant Republic, raising the Montfleurois levies that had once served alongside the Hetmantate against them. 

Although the initial years of the war saw consistent blows dealt to the republic and kingdom by the forces of Hetmanate, with raids and skirmishes making up the majority of the years from 1528-1530, morale was damaged among the Hetmanate as the financial coffers of the Samnäar dynasty began to dry out, furthermore, extensive campaigns into the inner regions of Montfleur proved disastrous for the Hetmanate whose older raiding tactics were easily repelled by fortifications and early cannon warfare thus forcing them to primarily battlefield conflicts, exposing their once rugged abilities to Montfleurois knights.

In 1531 a peasants revolt would force the Samnäar dynasty to refocus their forces internally, providing a gap for the Montfleurois and the Merchant Republic to reverse the frontlines directly into hetmanate territory, with the hopes of subduing the renegade Samnäar dynasty and forcing a peace.

The push by the Merchant Republic and Montfleur would succeed and by 1532 following a lengthy siege against the Hetmanate capital of Gossen, the hetmanate would enter into negotiations which would see the lands partitioned between the Merchant Republic of Knygta and the Kingdom of Montfleur. 

The partition of Thýven would be an enduring scar on the legacy of the Hetmanate which would not fully be repaired politically nor socially until the 1754 constitution which finally saw the nobles of Thýven recognised as a distinct founding entity of Rosenmarkke, as a result the region of Thýven would widely in the 14th-16th centuries be seen as a wild frontierland dominated by the Hetmanate, though it would become home to some of the nation's wealthiest fur trappers and traders.

Following the partition Montfleur and the Merchant Republic of Knygta would continue to exist as two politically distinct entities, though the marriage in 1516 and birth of Prince (and future king) Henri XII in 1518 and  princess (the future dogesse of the Merchant Republic) Catherine in 1559 would see the two nations gradually begin to converge their political foundations.

Amongst the earliest of these convergences would be the 1523 and 1534 state councils which would prove to be proto-triumvirate bodies, though more noble oriented and heavily feudalistic in terms of their organisation. These councils would be part fair and part diplomacy, securing trade and legal deals across the various ranks of nobility in both nations. 

Of the most notable of these state councils was the 1557 state council which would lead to the agreement on religious unity, with the papacy granting assent to the unification of the various dioceses within the two states to form a single recognised Knygta-Montfleur order of mass and service. 

However, as the 1560s arrived, tensions began to arise along the lines of the partition of Thýven, with the Merchant Republic controversially granting members of the hetmanate seats in the 1563 ducal conclave to elect the new doge following the death of the doge Piter Mandonii-Dargent in 1562. 

Such a move stirred fear within the Montfleuroise nobility, who were primarily concerned with a potential insurgency among the partitioned regions within their own borders, as a result the newly ascendant Henri XII would summon the Council of Estates of 1563, notably including the hetmanate representatives within Montfleur to debate the rights of the landowning hetmen of Montfleurois Thýven, the council would be contentious on many levels primarily due to the conquered status of the Hetmanate, with many nobles fearing that granting any formal rights or territorial recognition would undermine the very necessary reason for partitioning the hetmanate. 

As a result, for the sake of peace, the government of Montfleur and the nobles associated therein formally include the Thývenic nobility between both countries, and united the countries, using the marriage prior as a justification to do so, making the state of Grande Montfleur.

Unfortunately peace would not be long, for 80 years later the region once again was divided by the conflict known as the Montfleurois civil war, where pretenders to the throne of Montfleur took it and split the country into two places, one to place those traitors who supported the rightful heirs to the throne, and the other and heartland of Montfleur, for the loyalists.

This civil war left a scar in the territory, which remains to this day, and for the longest time was seen as impossible; however, as history proves, there indeed is a possibility for reunification.

 - Louis de Courville (Historian at the University of Valcur)
